name: Pootharekulu (Paper Sweet)
instructions: 1. Soak the Jaya rice for several hours and grind it into a very thin, watery batter.
2. Prepare an inverted clay pot (pot-pan) over a wood fire and apply a thin layer of cloth to the surface.
3. Dip a fine cloth into the rice batter and quickly smear it across the hot, inverted pot to create a translucent, paper-thin sheet.
4. Once the sheet dries and peels off, carefully lift it and keep it aside.
5. Place the wafer on a flat surface, sprinkle generous amounts of powdered jaggery, cardamom powder, and ghee.
6. Roll the paper-thin sheet into a cylindrical shape and set aside to cool.
description: Pootharekulu, originating from the village of Atreyapuram, is a traditional sweet often referred to as 'paper sweet' due to its delicate, translucent appearance. It is a labor-intensive delicacy frequently served during festivals, weddings, and special occasions in Andhra Pradesh, representing the artisanal skill of local sweet makers.
